title: Simulation Engineer - Drone Physical Models Integration
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As our GNC, ML, Embedded Software, and Validation teams scale, they rely increasingly on simulation to develop and test our autonomous defense systems. The value of that simulation depends directly on how faithfully it reproduces the real behavior of our drones.

Joining the Tooling team, you will be responsible for bringing the physical models of our drones into the simulator—including aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems. Designed by expert domain teams, these models require your expertise to translate user needs, integrate models into the simulator software stack, and validate expected behavior. Because not every use case requires the same level of realism, you will help establish the appropriate fidelity targets across applications.

This role offers high ownership and the opportunity to work at the intersection of physics, software engineering, and AI robotics with direct mission impact.

Responsibilities

  • Coordination with Domain Experts: Work with the teams in charge of aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems to understand their models, their assumptions, and their inputs and outputs, and to agree on how they are delivered to the simulator.

  • Model Integration: Integrate these models into the simulator software stack in a clean, performant, and maintainable way, with clear interfaces and configurable parameters.

  • Validation: Define and run tests that check the integrated models against the reference data given by the expert teams (flight logs, bench tests, manufacturer data), and report discrepancies back to the model owners.

  • User Needs & Fidelity Targets: Work with the simulator users (GNC, Embedded, Validation) to understand their use cases, and translate them into a realism target for each model. Pick the right balance between fidelity, performance, and integration effort, and prioritise the model integration work to match.

  • Documentation & Standards: Document the integrated models, their parameters, validity domains, and validation results, and help standardise the model integration and validation process.

Candidate requirements

  • Experience: Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in software engineering, simulation, or a related engineering field.

  • Physics Understanding: Good understanding of flight dynamics and enough physics background to discuss models with experts in aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems, and to turn their models into working code.

The Role...

As Social & Community Director, you will own the success and growth of Esquire’s social platforms, with a particular focus on Instagram and TikTok. This is a highly visible editorial role. You will be a host and voice for Esquire, fronting social formats and video content and representing the brand with audiences, partners and at key cultural, brand and membership events.

You will also help shape and grow Esquire’s new membership communities, hosting events, contributing to newsletters and working closely with the audience team to engage, nurture and build an active and connected community.

Main Duties...

  • Set Esquire’s social strategy across Instagram and TikTok, in line with the brand and wider editorial plans. Define clear audience priorities, content pillars and measures of success, adapting the approach as platforms, behaviours and audience habits evolve.
  • Grow Esquire’s following and engagement in ways that build meaningful, lasting audience relationships. Use analytics, social listening and audience feedback to understand what is working, decide what to make next and continually improve performance.

  • Conceive, host and support events that bring Esquire’s audience together. Work with editorial and commercial colleagues to shape the right experiences, host or moderate conversations and extend their value through social coverage.
  • Represent Esquire at selected partner, industry and audience events, acting as a highly visible ambassador for the brand and protecting the trust audiences place in Esquire by upholding its editorial and brand standards.
  • Set direction and priorities for colleagues and contributors working across social. Coach on-camera talent, build a strong and reliable network of contributors and work with the hubbed Social Media Executive to support Facebook targets.

What We Are Looking For...

Essential

Desirable

title: Software Engineer, Research Platform
descriptionHtml:
Software Engineer, Research Platform

About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData and our Trillion Gene Atlas (TGA), the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Software Engineer, Research Platform to join our team in London, embedded in our AI, genomics and computational biology teams. Your goal is to accelerate their research by bringing production-grade engineering to the systems they depend on.

This is an embedded role. You'll sit with the scientists, understand what they are trying to find out, and build the systems that get them there faster: making research code reliable, reproducible and fast; designing data pipelines and workflows that run at the scale of BaseData and the Trillion Gene Atlas; and building the tools and infrastructure that let a small research team run far more experiments. You'll move between genomics, computational biology and ML work as the research requires, and own what you build end to end.

The engineering problems are substantial: petascale biological data, workflows that span cloud and HPC, and research that is often limited by how quickly an idea can be turned into a result.

You'll report to the Head of Platform as part of our engineering team, which spans London and Boston, and work day to day within the AI research, genomics and computational biology teams in London.

About you

  • A very strong engineering background: complex production systems you have designed, built and owned. Expert in Python; strong habits around testing, code review and CI/CD.

  • You take responsibility for the outcome. If that means learning something new or working outside your usual area, you do it.

  • A solid understanding of data pipelines, workflow orchestration, distributed execution and scalable compute (Kubernetes, HPC, containers).

  • You can take a researcher's code, understand the question behind it, and make it robust without losing what made it useful.

  • A real interest in biology, ideally with experience of genomic, protein or sequencing data. You will learn the science well enough to understand the research, not just its code.

  • Collaborative and low ego. We care about drive, and in a small team everyone depends on what you build.

Nice to have

  • Research or applied experience in computational biology, bioinformatics or genomics.

  • Experience with bioinformatics tooling and sequencing data at scale.

  • Familiarity with Dagster or similar orchestration, Kubernetes, cloud and HPC compute.

  • Experience building tools, MCP servers or workflows that AI agents and researchers use to run computational experiments.

What we offer in return

Impactful Mission: This is a rare chance to do work that genuinely matters. You'll join a talented, fast-moving team, access unique biological datasets at scale, and see your contributions shape real breakthroughs in AI and curative therapeutics.

Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

High Growth: We truly believe in investing in our top talent, we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike to work scheme, life insurance, and more.

Do you want to join our team as our new Software Engineer, Research Platform? Then we'd love to hear from you.

We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

title: Staff Applied AI Researcher (Agentic Search)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast-growing team building an agent-native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google search, but for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing these systems to search and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval, ranking and passage extraction under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24/7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production. In the first year, you will own a specific part of the search stack, e.g. ranking or iterative retrieval.

What you'll work on:

  • Designing an agent-native search system that handles everything from low-latency single-hop search to complex deep search tasks requiring iterative planning, querying, refinement and reasoning.

  • Training ranking and retrieval models optimized for agent-driven workflows under real world constraints

  • Bringing the latest advances from the research community to our search stack and ship it to production.

Your responsibilities:

  • Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

  • Design and evolve multi-stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, retrieval, reranking and iterative retrieval)

  • Lead experimentation on modern retrieval approaches (embedding research, sparse and hybrid retrieval, reranking, context compression) and bring them into production

  • Develop methods for grounding LLMs in real-time web data at scale, using trust, quality and freshness signals to surface reliable sources

  • Partner with the evaluation team to define new metrics for agentic systems, where correctness is not reducible to clicks

  • Analyze trade-offs across relevance, latency, and cost, and work closely with engineering to deploy systems that operate at web scale

  • Mentor researchers and engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

Must haves:

  • 8+ years of experience in applied AI, ML, or software engineering

  • Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

  • Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking or building RAG-based assistants

  • Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

  • Experience with LLM-integrated or knowledge-intensive systems

  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

  • Strong programming skills in Python

  • Top-tier publications (ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, AAAI, EMNLP, ACL)

  • Ability to operate in a fast-moving, product-driven environment with high ownership and autonomy

Nice to haves

  • Background in agentic AI systems (agents, tool use, autonomous workflows)

  • Experience with RL post-training of LLMs or VLMs

title: Staff Applied Scientist, Location Intelligence
descriptionHtml:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Every parcel ends at a door. Where that door is, where a courier can park, and which way they walk in decide whether a handover takes seconds or minutes, and whether anyone ends up at the wrong place at all. Most of that never shows up on a map.

Relay sees the last mile through couriers' own devices: GPS traces from live deliveries that show where they park, which entrance they use and how long each handover takes. Turning those traces into a trusted picture of the real last mile is the foundation the rest of our Science builds on.

Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. Location intelligence is where it starts.

Location Intelligence Highlights

  • Telematics from the couriers who deliver for us: GPS traces, stops, parking spots and building entrances, all from live deliveries.

  • Mapping and road networks: where addresses and front doors really are, and how roads and traffic really behave.

  • A foundation layer: your work feeds routing, optimisation and courier intelligence, and gives our decision teams the evidence to tell a wrong address from a failed handover.

  • One of the first hires into Relay's new Location Intelligence team, with room to set the direction.

The Opportunity

As a Staff Applied Scientist, Location Intelligence at Relay, you'll:

  • Lead location intelligence at Relay, turning telematics and map data into a trusted picture of where deliveries really happen.

  • Build the methods that find the front door: map matching, stop and dwell detection, and parking and entrance inference from messy GPS traces.

  • Model road networks, traffic and travel times, so routes and plans reflect how the city really moves.

  • Take models from prototype to production, and own their quality once they are live.

  • Partner with Operational Research, Courier Intelligence and Engineering so correct addresses and doors flow into routing and decisions.

  • Raise the standard for location science at Relay, and grow the team, the research culture and our voice in the tech community.

We're looking for candidates who…

  • Have hands-on experience with telematics or GPS data: individual traces, map matching, and stop or dwell detection.

  • Have worked on a mapping or location product, whether an online maps platform or an internal mapping product for a delivery or mobility app.

  • Come from a STEM background, with strong statistics and solid data and coding fundamentals.

  • Have shipped location models into production, and owned them after launch.

  • Have set technical direction that others worked to, and brought people with them.

  • Collaborate generously, and explain complex ideas simply.

Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

5. Your peers trust your judgment. When you push for quality, people listen.

Interview Process

We understand that interviewing for a new role is both time and energy consuming–we aim to be thorough, speedy and transparent in our approach. You should expect for the entire 
process to be no more than 4 weeks from start to finish. You’ll meet with various members of our team and have the opportunity to fully validate that Fin and the role is the right fit
for you.

Unleash Your Potential

title: Stage de recherche : la place des SHS dans la recherche en école d’ingénieurs
department: Sciences humaines et sociales et Linguistiques
descriptionHtml:
Unité : Département Management International, IMT Nord Europe ; IMT Business School, Evry

Responsable hiérarchique : Clément Séhier, Jean-Luc Moriceau

Responsable fonctionnel : Clément Séhier, Jean-Luc Moriceau

Catégorie : Stagiaire (Master 1 ou Master 2)

Nature de l’emploi : Stage de recherche

Lieu de travail : IMT Nord Europe, campus de Villeneuve d’Ascq, ou IMT Business School, campus d’Évry

Contexte :

École sous tutelle du ministère de l’économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique, IMT Nord Europe est née en 2017 de la fusion de Télécom Lille et de l’École des Mines de Douai. Elle compte aujourd’hui parmi les plus Grandes Écoles d’ingénieurs au Nord de Paris avec plus 2200 élèves, dont un quart d’apprentis, plus de 600 diplômés par an et un réseau de 15 000 diplômés. Elle fait partie de l’Institut Mines Télécom, premier groupe public de Grandes Écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France, et est partenaire de l’université de Lille.

IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l’innovation et les créations d’entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l’Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1H30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l’ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l’ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d’enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s’appuie sur plus de 20 000 m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d’excellence dans les trois domaines « Systèmes Numériques », « Energie Environnement » et « Matériaux et Procédés ».

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l’École : www.imt-nord-europe.fr

Le stage est à pourvoir au sein du Département Management International d’IMT Nord Europe (campus de Villeneuve d’Ascq) ou à IMT Business School (campus d’Évry), en lien avec les enseignants-chercheurs en SHS du groupe IMT et avec la direction scientifique de l’IMT.

Missions :

Les écoles d’ingénieurs sont encouragées à développer des projets de recherche interdisciplinaires pour aborder des questions complexes, notamment celles liées aux transitions numériques, industrielles et socio-écologiques. Le stage porte sur la place des sciences humaines et sociales (SHS) dans la recherche en école d’ingénieurs, à travers une réflexion à la fois théorique et empirique sur l’ensemble des écoles de l’IMT.

Il s’agit non seulement de recenser des dispositifs, mais aussi d’interroger les conceptions de la recherche interdisciplinaire qu’ils traduisent, les conditions de leur développement et la place qu’y occupent les différentes disciplines et méthodes. Le stage contribuera à structurer les échanges entre les enseignants-chercheurs en SHS du groupe, à nourrir les réflexions de la direction scientifique et à éclairer la préparation du prochain plan stratégique (horizon 2028).

Activités :

  • Cartographier les compétences en SHS dans les écoles de l’IMT (chercheurs et chercheuses, disciplines, objets de recherche, méthodes), selon un périmètre défini avec l’encadrement.

  • Recenser les formes de collaboration interdisciplinaire impliquant des SHS (structures ou collectifs de recherche, autres dispositifs de coopération).

  • Analyser ces expériences : définition des questions de recherche, place des disciplines, méthodes, organisation du travail collectif, difficultés rencontrées et apports.

  • Comparer les pratiques du groupe IMT avec celles d’autres écoles d’ingénieurs.

  • Faire émerger des thématiques propices à l’interdisciplinarité, en particulier autour des transitions socio-écologiques.

  • Interroger les modes d’évaluation et de suivi de la recherche interdisciplinaire, et les relier à l’enseignement des SHS en école d’ingénieurs.

  • Mener une analyse documentaire et des entretiens semi-directifs avec des chercheurs (déplacements à prévoir entre plusieurs écoles du groupe).

  • Produire les livrables : cartographie, rapport et note de propositions ; restitution orale.


Profil du candidat/de la candidate : (Prérequis/ Diplôme) : étudiant·e de Master 1 ou 2 en SHS, LEA ou sciences de l’éducation.

Savoir-être

  • Autonomie et rigueur

  • Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs de disciplines différentes

  • Appétence pour la recherche théorique comme pour l’enquête qualitative

Savoir faire

  • Conduire des entretiens semi-directifs

  • Analyser des matériaux variés

  • Restituer les résultats de manière claire (rapport, note, présentation orale)

Connaissances

  • Intérêt pour les relations entre sciences, techniques et société

  • Interdisciplinarité, enseignement supérieur

  • Transitions socio-écologiques

Conditions :

Le stage est à pourvoir entre février et août 2027, pour une durée de 4 à 5 mois (stage de Master 1 ou 2). Les dates précises seront définies avec l’encadrement.

Renseignements et modalités de dépôt de candidature :

  • Pour tout renseignement sur le poste, merci de vous adresser à Clément Séhier, Département Management International ----- ou à Jean-Luc Moriceau -----

  • Pour tout renseignement administratif, merci de vous adresser à la Direction des Ressources Humaines : Par ailleurs, le poste peut être aménagé pour une personne en situation de handicap.

Date limite de candidature : 31/12/2026

title: Strategy & Operations Director
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Strategy & Operations Lead of Doit Lithuania, you will build and run the business in Lithuania and grow it across the European Economic Area.

You will be the first senior hire in Lithuania. You will own the regulatory relationship, the build of the team, the partner network and the launch. You will sit on the management board and lead the business day to day.

We’re looking for a generalist who learns quickly, thinks deeply, and enjoys solving difficult problems in a fast-moving, regulated environment.

What You’ll Own

  • Own the relationship with the Bank of Lithuania and other regulators.

  • Build the Vilnius team, including compliance, operations and control functions.

  • Select and negotiate with execution, custody, fund and banking partners.

  • Own the business plan, financial projections, capital plan and budget.

  • Launch the investment platform in Lithuania and roll it out across the EEA.

  • Set up governance, policies and controls that meet EU and Lithuanian requirements.

  • Work with group leadership on product, engineering and growth.

  • Report to the board and take ownership of business and regulatory outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • Generalist background in consulting, investment banking, start-ups, private equity or venture capital.

  • Experience building or scaling a business, ideally in financial services or fintech.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and business judgment.

  • Ability to learn regulation quickly and work credibly with regulators.

  • Strong ownership and execution skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with boards, regulators, partners and teams.

  • Comfortable working across product, operations, finance and compliance.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a senior manager.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

  • Curious, resourceful, and driven to build.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania.

  • Experience with MiFID II, brokerage, wealth management or fund distribution.

  • Experience building or running a regulated financial business in the EU.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.

  • People who avoid messy cross-functional problems.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

  • People who see regulation as someone else’s problem.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

Notre objectif est clair : aider les particuliers à réduire leurs factures énergétiques tout en participant activement à la transition énergétique. Et aujourd’hui on a besoin de toi pour propulser notre croissance !

Dans le cadre du lancement et du déploiement de nos pompes à chaleur en France, nous recherchons notre premier·ère Superviseur·ise CVC/HVAC pour superviser les installations de nos pompes à chaleur air-eau. Nous recherchons une personne passionnée, ayant de l’expérience dans l’installation de pompes à chaleur et/ou systèmes de chauffage et désireuse de nous aider à développer cette activité en France.

Il s’agit d’un poste sur le terrain couvrant la région d’Amiens, mais tu seras également amené·e à travailler depuis ton domicile ou depuis notre bureau de Lille lorsque cela sera nécessaire.


Ce que tu feras
- Tu nous aideras à mettre en place la structure technique de notre département dédié aux pompes à chaleur en France
- Tu veilleras à la qualité et au bon fonctionnement des installations réalisées par nos partenaires locaux
- Tu seras sur le terrain pour visiter les chantiers et t’assurer de leur bon déroulement
- Tu seras en mesure d’apporter une assistance technique pour résoudre directement tout problème identifié sur place
- Tu auras un esprit « dépanneur » pour trouver des solutions aux défis rencontrés et les résoudre à ton échelle
- Tu mettras à profit tes connaissances et ton expérience en matière d’installations de pompes à chaleur pour garantir une expérience fluide et exceptionnelle
- Tu conseilleras nos clients et tu les aideras à mettre en places les bonnes pratique de réduction des émissions carbone
- Tu examineras les cahiers des charges techniques et les plans techniques de nos pompes à chaleur, et tu pourras participer à leur élaboration/amélioration continue, en lien avec les équipes techniques & métiers du groupe
Profil recherché
- Tu as au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans l’installation et la maintenance de systèmes de pompes à chaleur aérothermiques
- Tu es disponible et prêt·e à te déplacer dans la région d’Amiens et le Nord de la France
- Tu es un·e technicien·ne expérimenté·e, notamment en plomberie et chauffage, et tu possèdes des connaissances en conception de systèmes de chauffage ; tu es en mesure de dépanner toi-même et d’intervenir techniquement sur place sur les chantiers
- Tu sais examiner et être force de proposition sur des cahiers des charges techniques ainsi que des plans mécaniques
- Tu as l'esprit entrepreneur : tu rejoins un nouveau projet où "tout est à faire". Tu n’as pas peur de partir d'une feuille blanche, tester, apprendre et avancer en autonomie.
- Tu es proactif·ve et rigoureux·se, tu sais organiser ton activité en autonomie, en optimisant au fur et à mesure, notamment en mettant en place des processus clairs et automatisés
- Tu as le goût du challenge, tu aimes aller sur le terrain ; tu n'as pas peur de te confronter aux artisans et de les aider à surmonter les irritants rencontrés. Doté·e d'un fort capital sympathie, tu sais fédérer tes interlocuteurs et les faire devenir de véritables ambassadeurs d’Octopus Energy !


Pré-requis & Qualifications

- Permis voiture en cours de validité
- Diplôme(s) de niveau CAP/BEP, ou VAE de niveau équivalent
- Avoir travaillé précédemment dans des entreprises certifiées RGE & Qualibat
- Maîtrise de l’anglais technique à l’écrit & l’oral (niveau B1-B2)
- Habilitation électrique (BR NF C18-510)

Ce sera également un plus si :
- Tu es à l’aise avec les outils & le numérique, notamment Excel
- Tu as de l’expérience avec la partie “électrique” des pompes à chaleur
- Tu possèdes l’habilitation électrique BR

Pourquoi tu vas adorer travailler pour nous ?

Tu as vu le salaire ou la fourchette prévu·e pour ce poste mais tu aimerais en discuter ? Demande-le nous ! Lors de notre premier contact, c’est un point que nous abordons toujours, car même si nous prenons soin de définir des grilles les plus justes possibles, il nous semble également important de faire correspondre ton expérience au bon salaire. Nous aurons l’occasion de t’en dire plus sur la manière dont nous avons défini le salaire et sur les autres avantages dont tu pourras bénéficier si tu nous rejoins ! Sache enfin que nous pouvons avoir un certain degré de flexibilité, car nous ne voudrions jamais que le salaire soit une raison pour laquelle quelqu’un·e ne postule pas chez Octopus - ce qui est le plus important pour nous est de trouver le bon Octofit !

Certifiée depuis 2024 et 4e en 2025, Octopus Energy France est classée 1ère sur plus de 200 entreprises au classement Great Place to Work 2026 ! Cela reflète bien notre engagement pour un environnement de travail épanouissant !

Nous sommes une organisation où les gens apprennent, décident et construisent plus rapidement. Où ils travaillent de manière autonome, avec des gens extraordinaires, sur des projets qui innovent. Intéressement au capital, flex-office, excellente mutuelle, forfait mobilité douce, prise en charge d’une partie de ton titre de transport au-delà du minimum légal, et même des jours de congés spéciaux pour t’investir dans un projet associatif qui te tient à coeur… Nous voulons que ton investissement soit récompensé par des avantages auxquels tu tiens vraiment !

Chez Octopus, nous cherchons des personnes foncièrement bienveillantes et empathiques. L’égalité des chances nous tient à cœur et nous veillons à offrir un environnement de travail inclusif et équitable. Nous t’invitons à postuler, quels que soient ton âge, genre, vie conjugale, couleur, handicap, grossesse ou parentalité, origine, convictions religieuses ou orientation sexuelle.

title: System Architect
descriptionHtml:
About Invisix

Semiconductor manufacturers can't build what they can't measure. Invisix Measuring Systems is a fast-growing scale-up in the high-tech industry, developing next-generation metrology solutions for the semiconductor sector. We work at the intersection of optics, software, and data.

We're a small team, but the depth of knowledge inside Invisix is anything but small. Our culture is professional and fast-paced, with short communication lines and a strong sense of shared purpose. Everyone here is committed, and everyone knows their work directly contributes to something bigger.

The Role

We're looking for a System Architect to decide what our metrology equipment is and why it's built that way: concept choices, system decomposition, budget allocations and the technology roadmap amongst others.

Reporting to our CTO, you look two to five years ahead and beyond, and shape our product line across several generations, so that what we build today still makes sense for our customers tomorrow. You work with our customers' technology roadmaps, marketing, the heads of R&D, our function architects and customer support, and you lead through persuasion rather than formal authority. Our system engineer builds on your concept and makes the current program work to spec. The role includes occasional travel to customers in Asia, the US and Europe.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the system architecture of our metrology product line, looking two to five years ahead and beyond, across several product generations

  • Make and justify the key concept choices, weighing physics, performance, cost and risk

  • Decompose the system into modules and interfaces, and allocate the key budgets, such as throughput, cost of goods, availability and performance

  • Translate our customers' technology roadmaps and future needs into product requirements, together with marketing and customers

  • Define our platform and reuse strategy, and decide which technologies we invest in

  • Align the heads of R&D and our function architects behind the architecture, and take on adjacent responsibilities as the company grows, such as representing Invisix in technical discussions with customers and partners

Is this you?

  • MSc or PhD in physics, applied physics, electrical or mechanical engineering or a related field, with at least 10 years of experience developing complex high-tech equipment, including a role as system or product architect

  • Experience in semiconductor equipment, for example lithography, metrology or inspection, or in comparable high-tech equipment, ideally with a product that made it to customers

  • Strong physics depth, in optics or measurement physics, so you can judge concept choices on their physical merits

  • Experience making architecture trade-offs across mechanics, electronics, optics and software, and setting system budgets for performance, throughput and cost

  • A preference for breadth over depth, comfort with ambiguity, the ability to make sound decisions on incomplete data, and the skill to persuade without formal authority

  • Active use of AI tooling in your daily work (concept studies, trade-off analysis, documentation) to boost efficiency

Nice to have

  • Experience working with the technology roadmaps of leading semiconductor manufacturers

  • Experience defining a product platform or reuse strategy across several generations

  • Experience balancing cost of goods and cost of service against performance

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up

What We Offer

  • A role at the heart of Invisix's product, shaping what our metrology equipment will be over several generations

  • Competitive salary and benefits, including an Employee Share Ownership Plan

  • A learning and development budget to support your growth

  • Flexible working arrangements, and room to grow into adjacent responsibilities as the team scales

Interested?

If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd like to hear from you, even if you only recognize yourself in part of this description. Submit your resume, and let's find out together if there's a match.

If this isn't quite the right position for you but you're still interested in Invisix, reach out to us at ----- style="color:#1F4E79">Diversity & Inclusion

We're committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, where ideas and individuals flourish. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and judge candidates on merit and potential contribution, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, disability, or other identity characteristics. What we're looking for is talent with integrity, a collaborative mindset, and a drive to make an impact.

Your Data

Your application data is processed by Invisix and kept in our applicant tracking system so we can consider you for this role and future opportunities. See our privacy policy for details: invisix.com/privacybeleid/

title: System Integration Senior Engineer (Platform Focus)
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

The System Integration Senior Engineer will help lead the Nyx system end‑to‑end integration and verification, with a focus on functional platforms (Software in the Loop Platform, Processor in the Loop Platform, Hardware in the Loop Platform, Functional Simulation Facility). You will define and execute test plans, manage requirement traceability, analyse test results, and close verification evidence across SIL/PIL/HIL and physical test campaigns. Working closely with subsystem leads, AIT teams, and external partners, you will identify integration risks, resolve anomalies, and ensure that all mechanical functions perform safely and reliably throughout the mission profile. This position requires a rigorous systems mindset, strong understanding of mechanical behaviour in the space environment, and the ability to lead multidisciplinary verification activities to successful closure.

Key Responsibilities

In your capacity a System Integration Senior Engineer, your role will continuously evolve, but initially your day-to-day duties will include:

  • Ensure the definition and implementation of the Nyx Earth system integration and verification activities, which meets technical and programmatic requirements and considers the adequacy of model philosophy, facilities availability, planning and costing.

  • Define plans and specifications with clear Success Criteria and support the generation of test procedures with the Functional Platform team.

  • Drive the technical discussions, preparation, organization and execution of the system verification campaigns, to ensure the closure of all system verification aspects, including nominal and off nominal spacecraft behaviors.

  • Organise the different reviews for incremental progress and ultimate closure of verification events.

  • Generate reports and drive the closure of the Items for Verification and Validation covered by the campaign.

  • Collaborate with all Functional Chain responsible and engineering disciplines to prepare and perform the system activities.

  • Process the anomalies occurring during the verification campaign in coordination with the Product Assurance Team and the rest of the Engineering Team.

What we would love to see from you

In the role of System Integration Senior Engineer ideally, you will have the following:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, or another related field.

  • 5 to 10 years of experience in systems design, analysis, and testing of aerospace or space-related systems, with a focus on integration of complex spacecraft and/or testing activities.

  • Hands-on hardware experience.

  • Practical experience / contact with functional test platforms, such as software in the loop, hardware in the loop, and bench testing.

  • Experience in the development and verification of space hardware.

  • Spacecraft systems knowledge.

Skills and Behaviours

  • Strong oral and written communication skills

  • Strong analysis and problem-solving skills

  • Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks

  • Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done

  • Ability to communicate at all levels of the business

  • Demonstrates behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork

  • Space enthusiast: ready to change the European space industry

  • Ability to thrive in a high paced development environment

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

title: Talent Partner, GTM
descriptionHtml:
Talent Partner, GTM

Location: London, onsite 4 days a week.
Duration: 12-month fixed term contract

Retire The ERP.

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers: automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. People don’t just use Light, they enjoy it.

We’re an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you’re excited to modernise how the world runs money, one workflow at a time, you’re in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we’re building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes.

Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

The Role

We plan to double the team in 2027. Most companies that grow this fast dilute the talent density that made them good. We won’t.

You’ll hire across GTM: the teams that win our customers and tell the world about Light. One week that might be an enterprise account executive, the next a product marketer or a demand generation lead. You’ll lead Marketing hiring and work alongside our Sales Talent Partner on Sales. It will be fast and at times messy, and you’ll be the person who brings structure to it.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to sit and screen all day. We want a guardian of the bar: someone who steps back, looks at the whole hiring problem and fixes what’s actually in the way. AI and good process handle the volume. You bring the judgement, and relationships with great people long before we need them.

What You’ll Do

  • Own Marketing hiring end to end, from individual contributors to leadership

  • Work on Sales searches alongside our Sales Talent Partner, including account executives, SDRs and partner sellers

  • Partner with Marketing and Sales leaders from the start: shape the role, challenge the brief, and build the scorecards and calibration that keep the bar high

  • Work out why a search is stalling, whether it’s the brief, comp, location, assessment or the market, and fix it. Sometimes the answer isn’t an external hire at all.

  • Map the markets for the GTM profiles we hire most often and build talent pools, so the pipeline exists before roles open

  • Hire internationally, with visa sponsorship and relocation support, as our GTM team expands into new markets

What Success Looks Like In Your First 6 Months

  • Marketing and Sales leaders bring you in early because you make their hiring decisions better

  • Hiring managers know what they’re getting and when, because you’ve told them, with data

  • We have mapped markets and warm talent pools for our most common Marketing and Sales profiles

  • Hires are closing at pace, and every one makes the team stronger

  • At least one AI workflow you’ve built is part of how the whole team works

How Our Talent Team Works

  • We protect talent density. Every hire should raise the average. We’d rather hold a role open a little longer than fill it with the wrong person.

  • We source proactively. Most of our best hires won’t apply, so we don’t wait for a role to open. We map the market, build relationships early and have a pipeline ready when the need arrives.

  • We use data. We know where candidates come from, where they drop out and what predicts a good hire. We use that to challenge hiring managers with evidence.

  • We build with AI. We don’t mean writing job ads with ChatGPT. We mean sourcing workflows, research agents and automations that change how much a recruiter can get done.

What You’ll Get From Us

Most Talent teams are bolting AI onto the way they’ve always worked. We’re building ours AI-first, from the ground up.

  • A team built AI-first. AI does the searching, research and admin, so you can spend your time on judgement, relationships and closing. You’ll help design how that works, rather than having it handed to you.

  • The tools and the time to build. You’ll have Claude, Codex, Lovable, Noon and Ashby from day one, plus a regular team build session to test new workflows. When something works, it becomes how the whole team operates.

  • A strategic role. You’ll help shape GTM hiring plans and market-entry decisions, bringing leadership evidence on where talent sits and what it costs.

  • Real ownership. Marketing hiring is yours to build from the ground up.

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years in Talent Acquisition, mostly in-house or in embedded or RPO-style roles, hiring GTM teams, including Marketing, in high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech

  • You switch gears fast. You can move from an enterprise sales search to a product marketing hire in the same afternoon, picking up the language, the market and what good looks like in each.

  • Deep knowledge of the London and European GTM talent market. Without opening LinkedIn, you could tell us which companies build the best Marketing and Sales teams, how they structure comp and OTE, and who’s likely to move.

  • You’re a guardian of the bar. You hold it under pressure, including telling a hiring manager “not this one” when the deadline is tight.

  • You step back before you dive in. When a search isn’t working, your first instinct is to work out why, before you screen more CVs.

  • You work at pace and bring structure to chaos. When priorities shift and reqs pile up, you set a clear plan and keep everyone moving.

  • A track record of proactive sourcing: hires you found and engaged before the role opened, rather than hires that applied

  • Hands-on experience building with AI to improve recruiting, with examples you can walk us through

Bonus Points

  • Hiring GTM teams for new markets

  • Building a Marketing team’s hiring from scratch

  • Experience with Claude, Codex, Lovable, Noon or similar tools

The Good Stuff

🏢 In-office culture, high talent density.
💸 Competitive salary.
🏝 25 days annual leave plus public holidays.
🚀 Shape how Light hires as we double the team.
🥳 Off-sites twice a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence!

Equal Opportunities

Light is an equal opportunities employer. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, just let us know.

title: Talent Partner
descriptionHtml:
I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

I started Anima to change that.

Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them.

If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

-- Shun

£60k–£100k base + bonus, plus equity
London, Farringdon · At least two days a week in the office

The role

Hiring is one of the biggest constraints on Anima’s growth. You’ll help unlock it by bringing outstanding people into the team and building the talent function that supports our next stage.

This is a chance to make talent your craft. Working closely with our founder and hiring managers, you’ll own searches and shape how we find, assess and win people. You'll have real responsibility and room to try things.

What you’ll do

  • Find outstanding people. Source promising candidates and build relationships with people who aren’t actively looking.

title: Teamleitung Naturnaher Wasserbau / Gewässerentwicklung (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Hier machst du dein Ding. Und wenn es passt, wird es auch deins.

Du planst Renaturierungen, Hochwasserschutz, Gewässerentwicklung. Fachlich macht dir so schnell keiner was vor. Was oft fehlt, ist der Raum dafür: Über dein Projekt entscheidet am Ende jemand, der nie am Gewässer stand, dein Budget verantwortest du nur auf dem Papier, und mit dem Kunden spricht jemand anderes.

Selbst wirksam werden. Bei Stowasserplan führst du dein eigenes Team, steuerst deinen Bereich wirtschaftlich und sprichst selbst mit deinen Auftraggebern. Du entscheidest, wie ihr arbeitet, und siehst direkt, was deine Entscheidungen bewirken. Nicht weil wir die besseren Ingenieure wären, sondern weil wir kurze Wege haben.

Schrittweise einsteigen. Wir suchen keine Führungskraft auf Zeit. Wer sich bei uns gut anstellt, unternehmerisch denkt und Verantwortung übernehmen will, kann sich nach einer Einarbeitungs- und Bewährungsphase am Unternehmen beteiligen und diese Beteiligung Schritt für Schritt ausbauen. So profitierst du direkt von dem Wert, den du mit deinem Team schaffst. Bei uns führt ein Weg von der Teamleitung zur Mitgesellschafterin oder zum Mitgesellschafter.

Wer wir sind

Stowasserplan plant seit 2009 naturnahen Wasserbau: Renaturierung von Fließgewässern, nachhaltiger Hochwasserschutz, Starkregen- und Erosionsvorsorge, Revitalisierung von Auen. Ingenieurbiologische Bauweisen sind unsere Kernkompetenz, nicht ein Zusatz im Leistungsverzeichnis.

Wie das aussieht, wenn es gelingt: Am renaturierten Pleißenbach spielen heute Kinder am Wasser. Am Hoyerswerdaer Schwarzwasser ist der Eisvogel zurück. Von der Machbarkeitsstudie über die Objektplanung nach HOAI bis zur Umweltbaubegleitung machen wir das komplett selbst.

Mit unserem Schwesterunternehmen Stowasserservice entwickeln wir aus unserer Praxiserfahrung Software, mit der andere Büros und Verwaltungen arbeiten: PROGEMIS für das Gewässermanagement, SOFIE für die Ingenieurbiologie. KI nutzen wir zunehmend als Werkzeug in unseren Planungsabläufen. Die fachliche Verantwortung bleibt beim Menschen.

Was du übernimmst

  • Ein Team von fünf bis acht Leuten: Projektverantwortliche, Projektmitarbeitende, Praktikanten. Du führst sie, planst Kapazitäten, führst die Mitarbeitergespräche und arbeitest neue Leute ein.
  • Die wirtschaftliche Steuerung deines Bereichs: Budgets, Termine, Qualität, Nachträge. Nach der Einarbeitung entscheidest du im vereinbarten Rahmen ohne Rücksprache.
  • Die Kundenbeziehung. Du sprichst selbst mit den Gewässerverantwortlichen in Städten und Verbänden, schreibst Angebote, verhandelst und holst Folgeaufträge.
  • Der Teil, für den uns heute die Zeit fehlt: KI-gestütztes Arbeiten in Prozesse einbauen, die halten. Projektstandards, Vorlagen, Qualitätssicherung, Wer das kann, prägt hier die nächsten Jahre.

Was du mitbringst

  • Führungserfahrung. Du hast mehrere Jahre eigenständig Projekte in Flussbau, Ingenieurbau, Wasserwirtschaft oder Regenwassermanagement geleitet und dabei Verantwortung für Menschen übernommen. Du weißt, wie man Aufgaben verteilt, Menschen entwickelt, Konflikte klärt und Entscheidungen auch dann trägt, wenn sie unbequem sind.
  • Du führst gern. Es macht dir Spaß, wenn dein Team besser wird, nicht nur, wenn dein Projekt gut läuft. Gespräche mit deinen Leuten siehst du als Teil deiner Arbeit, nicht als Unterbrechung. Begeisterte Kunden sind dein Maßstab.
  • Ein Studium im Bereich Bauingenieurwesen / Wasserbau, Landschaftsarchitektur, Umwelt- oder Landschaftsplanung oder etwas Vergleichbares.
  • HOAI sitzt, Baustelle ist dir vertraut, und im Vergaberecht (VgV, UVgO, VOB/A) kennst du dich sicher aus, als Bieter wie bei der Vorbereitung von Bauvergaben.
  • Praktische KI-Erfahrung. Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge bereits im Arbeitsalltag, etwa für Recherche, Texte, Auswertungen oder Angebote, kennst ihre Grenzen und hast Lust, das mit deinem Team weiterzuentwickeln.

Naturnahen Wasserbau und Ingenieurbiologie musst du nicht mitbringen. Das ist unser Kernwissen, und wir bringen es dir bei. Dafür nehmen wir uns Zeit und planen es ein.

Was du bekommst

  • Entscheidungen, die du triffst, statt Entscheidungen, die du vorbereitest.
  • 60.000 bis 70.000 Euro, je nach Erfahrung.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit, an ein bis zwei Tagen pro Woche im Homeoffice zu arbeiten.
  • Fortbildung, die wir bezahlen und für die du Arbeitszeit bekommst.
  • Ein Büro, das wächst. Wir gehen in die DACH-Region. Das schafft Aufgaben, die es heute noch nicht gibt.
  • Eine unternehmerische Perspektive: Wenn die Zusammenarbeit trägt, kannst du dich schrittweise am Unternehmen beteiligen.

Wir wachsen. Dafür bauen wir unseren Führungskreis aus und besetzen eine weitere Teamleitung in Vollzeit.

Du kommst nicht in ein fertiges Team, sondern in eines, das gerade neu sortiert und erweitert wird. Wer darin die Chance sieht, ist hier richtig.

title: Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services
descriptionHtml:
Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services

Hybrid in London (UK) or Remote within the UK

We’re looking for a Tech Lead to join the Funnel Platform team.

You’ll lead the team behind the shared services and frameworks that iwoca’s engineers build on. Those engineers are your customers, and the shared backend services feed iwoca’s lending decisions.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The Team

Funnel Platform takes its name from iwoca’s customer funnel – a business’s journey from first application to repeat lending. It owns the shared services and frameworks that the customer journey teams along that funnel build on, in the UK and Germany. The team’s aim is to make those services reliable, and simple for other teams to change.

The team works across three areas:

  • Credit data. Looking after the services that bring in data from the UK credit bureaus and Companies House.

  • Bank data. Looking after the service other teams use to work with business bank transactions.

  • New shared services. Building services that several teams need, including one for split tests.

The team is small – three backend engineers, including you. Infrastructure, such as Kubernetes and cloud hosting, sits with a separate team, so the work here is software.

The Role

As the Tech Lead in Funnel Platform, you’ll stay hands-on in the code while you lead the team. The team has no product manager, so you’ll decide what it builds, with input on priorities from the leaders of iwoca’s customer journey teams. You’ll report to the head of engineering for the customer journey teams.

  • Ownership. You’ll be accountable for the team’s existing services and the new ones it builds, from design to production.

  • Engineering standards. You’ll shape how the team designs and tests the shared services, and review the changes other teams make to them.

  • Impact. You’ll improve the services iwoca’s customer journey teams depend on, so your work speeds up theirs.

  • Influence. You’ll use data to persuade the customer journey teams and their leaders to back shared-service work that helps all of them.

  • Leadership and growth. You’ll line-manage the team’s two engineers, and give them the guidance and context to lead projects of their own.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Technical leadership. You’ve led engineers as a tech lead for around two years, while staying hands-on in the code.

  • Shared services. You’ve built and run backend services or frameworks that other engineering teams use and contribute to. You’ve reviewed their changes and shaped how they use your work.

  • Backend engineering. You know at least one backend language in depth, and you’ve designed and run distributed systems in production.

  • Problem finding. You’ve set a team’s priorities without a product manager, talking to the people who use your work to find the real problem before you design a fix. You can show what a technical trade-off costs or saves the business.

  • AI leverage. You’ve used AI to produce work you couldn’t have delivered without it – such as an internal tool or a migration. You know where it helps keep shared code easy to maintain, and you review what it produces before it goes live.

Bonus:

  • Python and Django. You’ve built production services in Python with Django.

  • Numerical background. You’re comfortable analysing data and drawing conclusions you can defend.

  • Experimentation. You’ve built tools that other teams use to run split tests.

  • Fintech. You’ve worked at a fintech or another financial services business.

The salary

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

title: Technical Instructional Designer (AI Programmes)
descriptionHtml:
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.

We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.

Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.

In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.

But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.

The opportunity

AI can draft a lesson in seconds. It can't tell you whether that lesson will actually land with a nervous career-switcher three weeks into an AI apprenticeship — or whether the concept it just explained is subtly, but fundamentally, flawed.

That's where you come in.

You'll be the human judgement layer sitting on top of our AI-assisted content pipeline — part subject-matter expert, part instructional designer. You'll decide what AI got right, fix what it didn't, and build the parts no AI can: the high-touch, high-stakes, deeply human moments in a learner's journey that make the difference between content that's technically correct and content that actually changes someone's career.

You'll have experience building content in generative and/or agentic AI — not just someone who's read about it, but someone who can explain it, question it, and know when the AI-generated explanation of tricky subjects is actually going to help a learner or quietly confuse them.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Design outcomes, not just content. Apply end-to-end backward design to build AI programmes and content where success is measured by what learners can do on the job — not just what they can pass a test on. You'll own the hardest part: turning a job-aligned outcome into content that actually gets learners there.

  • Chase real-world impact, relentlessly. When a piece of learning isn't landing — when an AI practitioner cohort isn't showing the outcomes it should — you won't wait to be told. You'll spot it, own it, and scope the revisions that bring it up to the standard it needs to hit.

  • Build what AI can't. Design the custom, high-touch programmes and creative assets — branching narratives, bespoke multimedia, high-stakes onboarding moments — that need real human empathy, creativity, and nuance. If AI could have built it, it's not your job; if only a person could, it is.

  • Put AI to work, deliberately. Use AI tools and prompt engineering to accelerate your own content development and uncover learning design approaches nobody's tried yet. This isn't about using AI because it's there — it's about knowing exactly where it earns its place.

  • Advise up, not just build. Work directly with Programme Designers and senior stakeholders on the quality and pedagogical effectiveness of the content you design. Your feedback doesn't stay in the room — it shapes how our rules, principles and frameworks evolve.

  • Prototype for the long game. Lead new learning formats and modalities that don't exist yet — and know how to balance shipping fast against building something sustainable enough to reuse.

     

What you'll bring

  • Real command of end-to-end ADDIE and backward design — you've built measurable, job-aligned outcomes and the assessments that prove learners hit them, not just theoretical frameworks on a CV.

  • A habit of treating "good enough" as a starting point, not a finish line — you notice when learning isn't driving real outcomes, and you take the initiative to fix it.

  • Genuine fluency with AI-powered tools and prompt engineering, used to accelerate content development and find genuinely new applications in learning design.

  • The ability to take a genuinely complex generative and/or agentic AI concept and design a learning experience around it that actually works — for a range of different learner personas

  • The confidence and track record to influence peers and senior stakeholders toward a specific, measurable curriculum improvement — not just raise a concern and move on.

  • Resilience when things don't go to plan — you can point to a time a project hit a real obstacle (a blocker, a shifting SME, a launch that missed the mark) and describe exactly what you did about it, and what you learned.

What gets you in the door

You'll need at least one of these:

  • Hands-on experience producing technical content for generative and/or agentic AI.

  • 2+ years designing instructional content in a commercial environment or for commercial clients.

  • Plus one of:

    • A Data or Computer Science degree (or close cousin of one)

    • Completion of a technical apprenticeship in Data or AI

    • 2+ years working as a practitioner in Data or AI

 

If you're a strong technical practitioner who's never formally studied instructional design, or a seasoned learning designer who's spent the last year deep in AI tools — either path can get you here. We're looking for the judgment, not a checklist.

 

What we'll actually explore together

We're upfront about what our process looks for, because we'd rather you come prepared to talk about the real thing than guess what we want to hear. Across the conversations, we'll dig into:

  • Advanced curriculum & applied design — how you turn an end-to-end backward-design process into measurable, job-aligned outcomes, and how you build creative assets that genuinely need a human touch.

  • Impact & excellence — what you do when a piece of learning isn't hitting its real-world mark, and how you weigh speed against building something built to last.

  • AI integration & innovation — where and how you've put AI tools and prompt engineering to work, and what that's actually unlocked.

  • Influence & stakeholder management — how you've moved a curriculum forward through a genuine disagreement or feedback conversation, not just delivered a good pitch.

  • Coachability & resilience — how you've handled a launch that didn't land, or a project blocker outside your control, and what you changed as a result.

Benefits

  • Time off - 27 days holiday, plus 5 additional days off: 1 life event day, 2 volunteer days, 2 company-wide wellbeing days (M-Powered Weekend) and 8 bank holidays per year

  • Health & Wellness- private medical Insurance with Bupa, a medical cashback scheme, life insurance, gym membership & wellness resources through Wellhub and access to Spill - all in one mental health support

  • Hybrid work offering - for most roles we collaborate in the office three days per week with the exception of Coaches and Instructors who collaborate in the office once a month

  • Work-from-anywhere scheme - you'll have the opportunity to work from anywhere, up to 10 days per year

  • Space to connect: Beyond the desk, we make time for weekly catch-ups, seasonal celebrations, and have a kitchen that’s always stocked!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).

For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

Providing false information is an offence and could result in the application being rejected or summary dismissal if the applicant has been selected, and possible referral to the police and the DBS.

title: Technical Support Manager | Working Student / Werkstudent (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Bei Superchat gestalten wir neu, wie Unternehmen mit ihren Kund:innen kommunizieren. KI wird dabei immer mehr zum Motor dieser Kommunikation. Integrationen sind das, was diesem Motor echte Power gibt: die Daten, Tools und Systeme, die aus einem cleveren AI-Agenten einen machen, der Prozesse wirklich automatisiert und Probleme löst.

Gegründet im Jahr 2020, ist Superchat heute die Plattform für über 10.000 Unternehmen weltweit - von bekannten Marken wie Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone und GASAG bis hin zu kleinen Unternehmen, Zahnarztpraxen und Solo-Founder:innen, die professioneller auftreten möchten.

Inzwischen laufen täglich Millionen von Nachrichten über Superchat.

Gestartet sind wir als Unified Inbox - ein zentraler Ort für alle Kommunikationskanäle wie WhatsApp, E-Mail, SMS oder Instagram. Mit dem Aufstieg von ChatGPT begann unser nächstes Kapitel: AI Agents, die über Chat, E-Mail und Voice in einer Qualität kommunizieren, die mit den besten menschlichen Teams mithalten kann.

Heute sind wir ein Team von rund 100 Mitarbeitenden, arbeiten profitabel und haben insgesamt 18 Millionen Euro Funding eingesammelt (unsere letzte Finanzierungsrunde liegt bereits 4,5 Jahre zurück - seitdem wachsen wir aus eigener Kraft weiter).

Unser Hauptsitz ist in Berlin. 

Als Werkstudent:in im Customer Support bist du die erste Anlaufstelle für unsere Kund:innen. Du löst ihre Anliegen im Live-Chat, koordinierst Eskalationen gemeinsam mit deinem Team und sorgst dafür, dass sich Unternehmen aus ganz unterschiedlichen Branchen und Regionen bei uns gut aufgehoben fühlen.

So könnte dein Tag aussehen:

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für die Bearbeitung von Kundenanfragen über unseren Live-Chat
  • Du bist die zentrale Eskalationsstelle und arbeitest eng mit deinem Team zusammen, um Kundenanliegen strukturiert zu koordinieren und zu lösen
  • Du betreust einen vielfältigen Kundenstamm aus verschiedenen Branchen und Regionen

Das bringst du mit:

  • Du bringst idealerweise Erfahrung im direkten Kundenkontakt und/oder Support mit und hast ein gutes technisches Verständnis, bestenfalls im B2B- oder SaaS-Umfeld
  • Du verfügst über Sprachkenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch (B2 - C2 level), sowohl schriftlich als auch mündlich
  • Du besitzt ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten, hohe Problemlösungskompetenz und Resilienz
  • Du arbeitest mit hoher Eigenverantwortung, proaktiv und bist motiviert

Why People Choose Us

  • Wir glauben an Zusammenarbeit vor Ort: Wir sind gerne gemeinsam im Berliner Office. Genau dort entstehen die besten Ideen, Entscheidungen werden schneller getroffen, wir lernen voneinander und wachsen als Team enger zusammen. Etwas Flexibilität für Remote Work bieten wir, aber unser Default und unsere Energie liegen im gemeinsamen Office-Alltag
  • Wir sind ein internationales Team mit unterschiedlichsten kulturellen Hintergründen und Sprachen - Offenheit, gegenseitiger Respekt und der Austausch verschiedener Perspektiven prägen unsere Zusammenarbeit
  • Wir schätzen Ambition und Motivation - wir suchen Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen, Initiative zeigen und Lust haben, sich schnell weiterzuentwickeln
  • Wir arbeiten mit hoher Eigenverantwortung und einer starken Lernmentalität - Fragen stellen, neugierig bleiben und sich kontinuierlich verbessern gehört bei uns dazu
  • Wir legen Wert auf Humbleness und Teamgeist - no Ego, offenes Feedback und die Bereitschaft voneinander zu lernen sind uns wichtiger als Titel

Benefits & culture

  • Regelmäßige Firmen- und Teamevents
  • Eine integrative und aufregende Start-up-Kultur, die schnelles berufliches und persönliches Wachstum ermöglicht
  • Schönes Büro im Herzen von Berlin (Prenzlauer Allee 242) mit kostenlosen Snacks, Getränken und bester Ausstattung

We want to build a community, not just a company.

Uns ist wichtig, ein Umfeld zu schaffen, in dem Menschen wirklich gerne Zeit miteinander verbringen - egal ob beim HYROX-Training, Golfen, Beer-Pong-Turnieren, Running Clubs, Warhammer, gemeinsamen Wochenendaktivitäten oder welcher Community auch immer du hier aufbauen möchtest!

Wir sind davon überzeugt, dass Diversität Unternehmen besser macht. Wir freuen uns über alle Bewerber:innen. Unabhängig von Gender, Herkunft, Nationalität oder Glaube. Fühl dich frei und schicke uns gerne deine Bewerbung!

Mit deiner Bewerbung stimmst du unseren Datenschutzrichtlinien zu.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung! 🙂
